questions.subject: Biology
questions.topic: ABO & Rh Blood Group Agglutination Assay
questions.questionText:
An individual with an unknown ABO blood group involved in an accident requires an emergency blood transfusion. A rapid laboratory agglutination assay yields the following results:
- Sample + Anti-A Serum: NO Agglutination
- Sample + Anti-B Serum: Agglutination Observed
- Sample + Anti-D (Rh) Serum: NO Agglutination
What is the precise blood group of this individual, and which blood type can be safely transfused in an emergency?

options.text: Blood Group B+; Can receive AB+ blood
Blood Group B-; Can receive B- or O- blood
Blood Group A-; Can receive A+ blood
Blood Group AB-; Can receive AB+ blood

questions.solutionExplanation: Agglutination with Anti-B serum confirms the presence of Antigen B. No agglutination with Anti-A serum confirms absence of Antigen A. No agglutination with Anti-D serum confirms the absence of Rh antigen (Rh-). The blood type is B- (B Negative). An Rh- recipient can safely receive blood only from Rh- donors (B- or universal donor O-).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
During a cardiac catheterization procedure, a cardiologist measures the following pressure and volume parameters in a patient's left ventricle:
- End-Diastolic Volume (EDV): 130 mL
- End-Systolic Volume (ESV): 50 mL
- Heart Rate (HR): 80 beats/min
What is the patient's Stroke Volume (SV) and total Cardiac Output (CO)?

options.text: SV = 180 mL; CO = 14.4 L/min
SV = 80 mL; CO = 6.4 L/min
SV = 50 mL; CO = 4.0 L/min
SV = 80 mL; CO = 4.0 L/min

questions.solutionExplanation:
1. Stroke Volume (SV) = EDV - ESV = 130 mL - 50 mL = 80 mL.
2. Cardiac Output (CO) = SV × HR = 80 mL × 80 bpm = 6400 mL/min = 6.4 L/min.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: An ECG trace recorded from an emergency patient suffering from chest pain demonstrates a marked, sustained elevation of the S-T segment above the baseline. What acute clinical condition does this specific ECG abnormality signify?

options.text: First-Degree Atrioventricular Block
Acute Myocardial Infarction (Heart Attack)
Atrial Fibrillation
Ventricular Extrasystole

questions.solutionExplanation: ST-segment elevation (STEMI) on a standard ECG is the diagnostic hallmark of transmural Acute Myocardial Infarction (Heart Attack), indicating acute ischemic necrosis of the ventricular myocardium.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: What is the physiological purpose of the 0.1-second conduction delay imposed by the Atrioventricular (AV) Node during electrical propagation through the heart?

options.text: To allow the lungs to fully oxygenate pulmonary venous blood
To ensure complete atrial contraction and ventricular filling before ventricular systole begins
To prevent semilunar valves from opening during atrial diastole
To allow Purkinje fibers to synthesize ATP via oxidative phosphorylation

questions.solutionExplanation: The AV node imposes a 0.1-second delay in electrical impulse transmission from atria to ventricles. This ensures that atrial contraction (Atrial Systole) completes its ejection of blood into the ventricles before the ventricles begin their contraction (Ventricular Systole).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: A patient with severe liver cirrhosis exhibits a marked drop in blood plasma protein synthesis. Which plasma protein deficiency directly leads to systemic peripheral edema (swelling) in this patient?

options.text: Deficiency of Fibrinogen leading to internal hemorrhage
Deficiency of Albumin causing a collapse in Colloid Osmotic Pressure (Oncotic Pressure)
Deficiency of γ-Globulins causing loss of cellular immunity
Deficiency of Prothrombinase causing capillary rupture

questions.solutionExplanation: Albumin synthesized by the liver is the primary plasma protein responsible for generating Colloid Osmotic Pressure (~25 mmHg) that retains fluid inside blood capillaries. Loss of albumin reduces oncotic pressure, allowing fluid to leak into interstitial spaces, causing systemic edema.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: During blood coagulation, which specific plasma enzyme complex converts the inactive zymogen Prothrombin (Factor II) into active Thrombin (Factor IIa) in the presence of Calcium ions (Ca²⁺)?

options.text: Hageman Factor (Factor XIIa)
Prothrombinase / Thrombokinase Complex
Transglutaminase (Factor XIIIa)
Plasminogen Activator

questions.solutionExplanation: The common clotting pathway culminates in the assembly of the Prothrombinase (Thrombokinase) Complex (comprising Factor Xa, Factor Va, phospholipids, and Ca²⁺), which converts inactive Prothrombin (Factor II) into active Thrombin (Factor IIa).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which blood vessel carries nutrient-rich blood absorbed from the stomach and intestines directly to the liver before it enters systemic circulation?

options.text: Hepatic Artery
Hepatic Portal Vein
Renal Portal Vein
Inferior Vena Cava

questions.solutionExplanation: The Hepatic Portal Vein drains blood from the capillary beds of the digestive tract (stomach, intestines, pancreas) and delivers it directly to the capillary sinusoids of the Liver, forming the Hepatic Portal System.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: What electrical event during the cardiac cycle corresponds to the QRS Complex on a standard ECG, and what mechanical event immediately follows it?

options.text: Atrial Depolarization; followed by Atrial Systole
Ventricular Depolarization; followed by Ventricular Systole
Ventricular Repolarization; followed by Joint Diastole
Atrial Repolarization; followed by Isovolumetric Relaxation

questions.solutionExplanation: The QRS Complex represents rapid Ventricular Depolarization. Ventricular contraction (Ventricular Systole) begins immediately after the Q wave and continues through the S-T segment.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: An Rh- mother is pregnant with her second Rh+ child. She was not administered RhoGAM (anti-D antibodies) after her first Rh+ pregnancy. Which class of maternal antibodies crosses the placenta to cause Erythroblastosis Fetalis in the fetus?

options.text: IgM antibodies (pentameric)
IgA antibodies (dimeric)
IgG antibodies (monomeric)
IgE antibodies (monomeric)

questions.solutionExplanation: Maternal anti-Rh antibodies produced following sensitization belong to the IgG class. IgG is the ONLY antibody class that can cross the placental barrier via FcRn receptors to enter fetal circulation and destroy fetal Rh+ erythrocytes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: What anatomical structure anchors the cusps of the Tricuspid and Bicuspid AV valves to the papillary muscles in the ventricular walls, preventing valvular prolapse during ventricular systole?

options.text: Purkinje Fibers
Chordae Tendineae
Trabeculae Carneae
Pectinate Muscles

questions.solutionExplanation: Chordae Tendineae are tough, fibrous cords that connect the free margins of the AV valve cusps (Tricuspid and Mitral) to the Papillary Muscles of the ventricular endocardium, preventing the valves from inverting into the atria during high-pressure ventricular contraction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements correctly characterize the Formed Elements of human blood? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Erythrocytes (RBCs) are biconcave, enucleated at maturity, and have an average lifespan of 120 days.
Neutrophils are the most abundant WBCs (60–65%) and function as phagocytes.
Basophils secrete Histamine, Heparin, and Serotonin to mediate inflammatory responses.
Thrombocytes (Platelets) are nucleated cells derived from lymphocytes in the spleen.

questions.solutionExplanation: A, B, C are correct: RBCs are biconcave/enucleate (120 d lifespan), Neutrophils are PMN phagocytes (60–65%), and Basophils release histamine/heparin/serotonin. D is incorrect: Platelets are ENUCLEATED cell fragments derived from bone marrow Megakaryocytes (NOT lymphocytes).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Select the valid statements regarding human cardiac mechanics and heart sounds: (Select all that apply)

options.text: The first heart sound ('LUB') is caused by the closure of the Tricuspid and Bicuspid (AV) valves at the start of ventricular systole.
The second heart sound ('DUP') is caused by the closure of the Semilunar valves at the start of ventricular diastole.
During Joint Diastole, all four heart chambers are relaxed, and blood flows passively from atria into ventricles.
Stroke Volume (SV) is defined as the total volume of blood in the heart at the end of diastole (EDV).

questions.solutionExplanation: A, B, C are correct: LUB = AV valve closure; DUP = Semilunar valve closure; Joint Diastole allows passive 70% ventricular filling. D is incorrect: Stroke Volume = EDV - ESV ≈ 70 mL (it is the volume ejected per beat, NOT total volume).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following physiological factors INCREASE Cardiac Output (CO)? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Sympathetic nervous stimulation releasing Noradrenaline at the SA Node
Secretion of Adrenaline and Noradrenaline from the Adrenal Medulla
Parasympathetic stimulation via the Vagus Nerve releasing Acetylcholine
An increase in End-Diastolic Volume (EDV) according to the Frank-Starling Law

questions.solutionExplanation: A, B, D are correct: Sympathetic stimulation, adrenal medullary hormones (adrenaline), and increased venous return (EDV) increase HR, contractility, and Stroke Volume, elevating Cardiac Output. C is incorrect: Parasympathetic (Vagus) stimulation DECREASES heart rate and cardiac output.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements regarding Lymph and the Lymphatic System are TRUE? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Lymph is a clear fluid containing plasma solutes and abundant lymphocytes, but lacks RBCs and platelets.
Dietary fats absorbed by intestinal villi are transported as chyle in specialized lymphatic capillaries called Lacteals.
Lymph drains back into the systemic circulation via the Subclavian Veins.
Lymphatic vessels contain internal valves to ensure unidirectional fluid flow toward the heart.

questions.solutionExplanation: All options are correct facts regarding lymph composition, fat absorption in lacteals, lymphatic drainage into subclavian veins, and unidirectional lymphatic valves.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Select the correct options regarding the Regulation of Cardiac Activity: (Select all that apply)

options.text: The cardiac center is located in the Medulla Oblongata of the brainstem.
Sympathetic nervous signals increase heart rate and the strength of ventricular contraction.
Parasympathetic signals transmitted via Cranial Nerve X (Vagus) decrease heart rate and conduction speed.
Thyroxine hormone from the thyroid gland decreases cardiac sensitivity to catecholamines.

questions.solutionExplanation: A, B, C are correct: Medulla controls cardiac center; Sympathetic accelerates HR/contractility; Vagus (parasympathetic) slows HR/conduction. D is incorrect: Thyroxine INCREASES heart rate and enhances cardiac sensitivity to catecholamines.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following conditions correctly match their pathophysiological descriptions? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Atherosclerosis → Plaque deposition (calcium, fat, cholesterol) in coronary arteries narrowing the lumen.
Angina Pectoris → Transient substernal chest pain caused by acute myocardial ischemia.
Heart Failure → Inability of the heart to pump blood effectively, often presenting with pulmonary congestion.
Hypertension → Persistent elevation of blood pressure above 140/90 mmHg.

questions.solutionExplanation: All options represent accurate etiology and clinical manifestations of major cardiovascular disorders.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which clotting factors require Vitamin K for their enzymatic synthesis in the liver? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Factor II (Prothrombin)
Factor VII (Proconvertin)
Factor IX (Christmas Factor)
Factor X (Stuart-Prower Factor)

questions.solutionExplanation: Vitamin K is a required co-factor for the hepatic γ-glutamyl carboxylase enzyme that post-translationally modifies Factors II, VII, IX, and X (mnemonic: 2 + 7 = 9, then 10).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Select the correct statements regarding Blood Vessel Histology: (Select all that apply)

options.text: Arteries possess a significantly thicker, more muscular Tunica Media than veins.
Veins contain internal valves to prevent backflow of low-pressure blood.
The Tunica Intima is composed of a simple squamous endothelial cell layer.
Capillary walls consist of all three layers: Tunica Intima, Tunica Media, and Tunica Externa.

questions.solutionExplanation: A, B, C are correct: Arteries have a thick tunica media; veins have internal valves; tunica intima is endothelium. D is incorrect: Capillaries consist ONLY of a single layer of endothelium (Tunica Intima) on a basement membrane; Tunica Media and Externa are absent.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following features characterize the ABO Blood Group System? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Blood Group O individuals are universal donors because their RBCs lack both A and B surface antigens.
Blood Group AB individuals are universal recipients because their plasma lacks both Anti-A and Anti-B antibodies.
The I^A and I^B alleles display codominance when present together (I^A I^B).
Anti-A and Anti-B antibodies are naturally occurring IgM antibodies that do not cross the placenta.

questions.solutionExplanation: All options are correct facts regarding ABO surface antigens, plasma antibodies, codominance, and universal donor/recipient status.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Select the correct options regarding the Human Nodal Conducting System: (Select all that apply)

options.text: The SA Node is located in the upper right wall of the Right Atrium.
The AV Node is located in the lower left corner of the Right Atrium near the atrioventricular septum.
Action potential conduction speed is fastest in Purkinje fibers (≈ 4 m/s) and slowest in the AV Node (≈ 0.05 m/s).
The AV Bundle (Bundle of His) is the only electrical connection between the atria and ventricles.

questions.solutionExplanation: All options represent true anatomical and electrophysiological facts regarding the human myogenic conducting system.
